messages:
Alex Chen: Quick sync — we need to lock the deploy pathways for Private (VPC/on-prem) by EOW. Customers keep asking about: in-place upgrades, IP preservation, and a low-touch installer. Can we surface tradeoffs and a proposed checklist?
Meera Patel: +1. Can we get a concise scope doc we can show field? I can pull the top 5 customer asks from the tracker. Link: https://go/priv-onramp-asks (draft)
Sam Torres: FYI constraints: kernel-level networking plugins vary across customer infra. For in-place upgrades we need a preflight that validates egress, ipam, and kube-proxy modes. Minimal flag set for installer: `--preserve-egress=true --ipam=customer`
Raj Kumar: For tenant IP preservation we have 3 viable patterns:
- nat-relay (no IP preservation but simplest)
- egress pin + DNAT (preserve external IPs but needs delicate firewall changes)
- BGP handoff (operator-assisted, best for large-scale customers)
Each has different rollback complexity.
Linda O'Neill: Also important: SLA/rollback windows. If we ship a rolling operator upgrade path we should commit to a 2-hour downgrade window and clear comms. Customers asked for an option to opt-out of automatic upgrades.
Meera Patel: Putting a short customer-facing matrix together: effort vs benefit for each pattern. Will share a one-pager.
Sam Torres: Suggest we propose three upgrade lanes for product: `safe-operator` (managed rolling with operator + canary), `in-place-minor` (db migration-free patches), `forklift` (full re-deploy for major infra changes). Each lane maps to networking pattern choices.
Alex Chen: Good. Let's map launch criteria per lane — e.g., for `safe-operator` we need: CI e2e passing on relabel tests, preflight >=95% success, rollback script tested. 
Raj Kumar: Important checklist items for netops: BGP session health checks, AS path validation, deterministic egress tests, and IP persistence verification. We should add a small `net-check` binary to installer.
deploy-bot: CI:priv-deploy-packaging #423 passed (smoke + net-check) — artifact: s3://redwood-builds/priv-2026-03-21.tar.gz
Linda O'Neill: Field asks: let customers toggle `automatic-upgrade: false` at tenant level, and we need an admin UI surface in Console to show upgrade progress and egress IP diffs.
Meera Patel: I'll draft the one-pager and a suggested customer comms blurb. Will also include the four golden signals we track for rollout quality.
Sam Torres: Quick tech note for the doc: include `installer --mode=slim` profile for airgap/minimal resource installs. Also include example `kustomize` overlay snippet in appendix.
Alex Chen: Action items: 1) Meera — one-pager with matrix + comms (EOD Thu). 2) Raj — net-check PoC and BGP testplan (Mon). 3) Sam — installer flag doc + slim profile (Mon). 4) Linda — SLA text and rollback window proposal (Mon).
Meera Patel: Any objections to proposing `safe-operator` as the default recommended path for greenfield customers?
Raj Kumar: No objections. Document that customers with strict IP preservation should expect operator-assisted or BGP lanes only.
Linda O'Neill: Agree. Also add 'opt-out' path in admin for automatic upgrades and an explicit acceptance checkbox for forklift migrations.
Alex Chen: Great. We'll reconvene next Wed for the draft review. If anyone wants to add concerns before I circulate the initial roadmap, ping me here. :thumbsup:
